transcript.text: The sides of our new fridge freezer get really warm, almost hot, especially near the front edge. Is that a fire risk? It's in an alcove between two units.

It is not a fire risk. Modern fridge-freezers dissipate heat through the condenser coils, which are often built into the side panels or the rear grille. However, because it is in an alcove, you must ensure there is adequate ventilation (usually at least 5cm of space on all sides) so this heat can escape. If the sides are scorching hot and the appliance smells of burning plastic or trips your electricity, stop using it immediately.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Thanks, that's reassuring. There's no burning smell and it hasn't tripped anything. The gap is only about 1cm each side though, so is that a problem?

A 1cm gap is most likely too tight. The condenser needs airflow to dissipate that heat; without it, the appliance works harder and the sides can become uncomfortably hot or even trigger a safety shutdown. Please pull the unit out to create at least 5cm of clearance on all sides and check if the warmth reduces after a few hours of running.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I'd rather not pull it out, we've just had new flooring laid and I'm worried about scratching it. Is there any other way to sort the gap, or check what the manual says? I do have the manual for it.

Since moving it is not an option right now, the best step is to check the manufacturer's specific guidance in your manual. Some modern fridge-freezers are designed with 'zero-clearance' or low-gap installation options where heat is vented through the top or bottom rather than the sides; if yours is one of these, 1cm might be acceptable. If the manual requires more space (typically around 5cm), you will need to find a way to create that gap—perhaps by using a thin spacer or adjusting the alcove—to prevent long-term overheating and energy waste.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
The manual says to leave space but I haven't checked the exact figure. The model is H7X 93T SK, if that helps. What should I be looking for in the manual?

That model number looks like a Neff series, which often uses the sides for heat exchange. In your manual, look specifically at the 'Installation' or 'Technical Data' section. It will state the required clearance—typically 5cm is standard for freestanding units where sides dissipate heat. If it specifies 5cm, then 1cm is most likely too tight and the sides will overheat. If it mentions a lower figure (like 0-2cm) or says 'suitable for built-in use', then your installation might be correct despite the warmth.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

Thanks. It's actually a Hotpoint, not a Neff, if that changes anything. I'll look in the manual's installation section, but the sides stay warm to hot all the time, though I can keep my hand on them. Is that normal for this type?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes, that is normal for this type of fridge-freezer. The sides contain the condenser coils which remove heat from inside; they are designed to get warm or even hot during operation. Because your unit is in an alcove with only 1cm gaps, the heat cannot escape efficiently, so it stays hotter than it would if there were more space. As long as there is no burning smell and it isn't tripping the electricity, this is not a fault or fire risk.

Insufficient clearance due to alcove installation (medium)
